mainTopic: Oil sales: profit limits, deductions for sediment and absorption, mixing sediment, residue, and a guard who moves a deposited barrel
overview: The גמרא first works out the math of רב יהודה's oil sale. It then shows that his profit fits שמואל's rule that a seller may profit up to one-sixth: the barrel and the sediment he keeps add to his profit, and his labor and the cost of the tap balance it out. Next it returns to the משנה and explains why an old cask counts as absorbing no oil. רב נחמן says the משנה means casks coated with pitch, and אביי says a cask that is already soaked takes in no more. אביי then ties the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about sediment to whether a seller may mix sediment into oil, and he defends רבי יהודה's view using the משנה about selling a צמד. רב פפא reverses אביי's reading of both sides. A ברייתא then compares a buyer and a depositor regarding residue, and the גמרא settles a contradiction by separating a buyer who paid in תשרי from one who paid in ניסן. Finally, a new משנה rules on a guard who moves a deposited barrel that then breaks. The גמרא says it follows רבי ישמעאל, who holds that an item can be returned without the owner knowing. רבי עקיבא's opposing view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Working out the math of רב יהודה's oil sale
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא calculates רב יהודה's profit. Thirty-six pitchers sold at six each cover his cost, twelve are left over, and eight of those are lost to absorption, which leaves four pitchers of profit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take away the thirty-six pitchers sold at six each, and twelve are left. Take away eight for the one-sixth that the barrel soaks up, and four are left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is doing the arithmetic on the oil sale of רב יהודה that was described just before. It wants to see exactly how much he earned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first thirty-six pitchers only pay back what he spent on the barrel. Out of the twelve that remain, eight are counted as the one-sixth that soaks into the barrel. Only four pitchers end up as real profit.

keyTerms.meaning: Sixths, here the one-sixth lost to absorption

phrases.english: Subtract thirty-six sold for six each,
phrases.notes: These are the pitchers whose sale pays back what he spent on the barrel.

phrases.english: twelve remain for him.
Subtract eight for the sixths,
phrases.notes: Eight is one-sixth of the whole barrel, the amount the barrel soaks up.

phrases.english: four remain for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב יהודה's oil sale from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה's net profit comes to four pitchers.

steps.title: שמואל allows profit up to one-sixth, so why was his profit so small?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings שמואל's rule that a seller may profit up to one-sixth. Four pitchers is much less than that, so why did רב יהודה not charge more?
steps.simpleTranslation: But שמואל said: someone who makes a profit should not profit more than one-sixth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the calculation using שמואל's rule. That rule implies a seller may take a full one-sixth profit, yet רב יהודה took much less.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's limit tells us that up to one-sixth is allowed. Four pitchers out of a large barrel is far below one-sixth. So the math does not seem to match how a seller would normally price his goods.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say, a phrase that opens a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: Here the challenge is that רב יהודה's profit looks too LOW. It is not saying the profit was too high. That opposite question comes later, in step 4.

phrases.english: But didn't שמואל say:

phrases.aramaic: הַמִּשְׂתַּכֵּר אַל יִשְׂתַּכֵּר יוֹתֵר עַל שְׁתוּת!
phrases.english: one who profits should not profit more than one-sixth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the profit figure worked out in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The four-pitcher profit calculated in step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל allows a profit of up to one-sixth, and four pitchers falls far short of that.

steps.title: The barrel and the sediment add to his profit
steps.stepSummary: Answer: רב יהודה also keeps the empty barrel and the sediment, and these add to his profit.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is the barrel and the sediment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the four pitchers are not his whole profit. He also keeps the barrel itself and the sediment at the bottom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He bought the barrel together with everything inside it. After the oil is sold, the barrel and the sediment still belong to him and are worth something. So his real profit is bigger than four pitchers.

keyTerms.meaning: Sediment, the dregs at the bottom

phrases.english: There are the barrels and the sediment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds parts of the profit that were left out of the count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His profit was only four pitchers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel and sediment he keeps raise his profit.

steps.title: Then his profit is now more than one-sixth
steps.stepSummary: If we add the barrel and the sediment, the profit seems to go over the one-sixth limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he ends up with more than one-sixth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. Adding the barrel and sediment now seems to make the profit too big.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the profit looked too small. Once the barrel and sediment are added, it seems to pass שמואל's one-sixth limit. That would mean רב יהודה overcharged.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי נְפִישׁ לֵיהּ טְפֵי מִשְּׁתוּת?
phrases.english: If so, he has more than one-sixth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי נְפִישׁ לֵיהּ טְפֵי מִשְּׁתוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the barrel and sediment add to the profit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting them makes the profit go over שמואל's one-sixth limit.

steps.title: His labor and the tap cost balance it out
steps.stepSummary: Answer: we must also count his effort in selling and the payment for putting a tap in the barrel. With these included, the profit comes out exactly right.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is his effort, and the payment for tapping the barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה also had costs. He put work into selling, and he had to pay someone to put a tap in the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These costs take away from the extra value of the barrel and sediment. Once they are counted, his profit lands within the one-sixth limit. So the sale was fair on both counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The payment for tapping, for putting a tap in the barrel

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's profit fits שמואל's one-sixth rule. The barrel and sediment raise the profit, and his labor and the tap cost bring it back down.

phrases.english: There is his effort and the payment for tapping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Subtracts costs that were left out of the count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel and sediment push the profit over one-sixth.
steps.terutzMaskana: His labor and the tap cost balance it out, so the profit is allowed.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about refined oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. It says that with refined oil, the seller does not take anything off for sediment, and the rest of that ruling continues from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was refined oil, he does not take anything off for sediment, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. This is setting up the question that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and so on' point to the rest of the משנה's ruling. That part says that oil stored in old, already-soaked casks gets nothing taken off for absorption. The next question is about that part.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on, meaning the rest of the quote

phrases.english: If it was refined oil,
he does not take anything off for sediment, and so on.
phrases.notes: The 'and so on' points to the rest of the משנה: with old, soaked casks, nothing is taken off for absorption.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיָה שֶׁמֶן מְזוּקָּק אֵינוֹ יוֹצִיא לוֹ שְׁמָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With refined oil, nothing is taken off for sediment, and with old casks nothing is taken off for absorption.

steps.title: Surely every cask absorbs some oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a cask, even an old one, could absorb no oil at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is impossible that it doesn't absorb anything!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling about old casks. It seems that some oil must always soak into the cask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when the casks are old, the seller may not take anything off for absorption. But common sense says a cask always soaks up at least a little. So why should the seller have to carry that loss with no deduction?

phrases.english: But it is impossible that it doesn't absorb!
phrases.notes: This is about the old casks from the rest of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that nothing is taken off for absorption with old casks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any cask must soak up at least a little oil.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the משנה is talking about casks coated with pitch
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה is speaking about casks lined with pitch. An old cask coated this way absorbs nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: they taught this about casks coated with pitch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers by narrowing the case. The משנה is talking only about casks lined with pitch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pitch seals the walls of the cask. An old, pitch-coated cask truly takes in no oil, so the משנה's ruling makes sense for that kind of cask.

keyTerms.meaning: Coated with pitch, sealed with זפת
They taught, here meaning the משנה

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
They taught it about casks coated with pitch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is talking about any old cask.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is talking only about old casks coated with pitch.

steps.title: אביי: a soaked cask absorbs no more
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that even without pitch, a cask that is already full of soaked-in oil takes in no more.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: even if you say it is not about pitch-coated casks, once they are soaked, they are soaked.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer. He says the משנה can be talking even about casks without pitch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An old cask has already soaked up all the oil it can hold, so it cannot take in any more. Unlike רב נחמן, אביי does not need to narrow the משנה to pitch-coated casks.

keyTerms.meaning: Once they are soaked, they are soaked

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why old casks count as absorbing nothing. רב נחמן says they are coated with pitch. אביי says an already-soaked cask takes in no more.

phrases.english: אביי said:
Even if you say it is not about pitch-coated casks,
once they are soaked, they are soaked.
phrases.notes: In other words, the cask is already full of oil in its walls, so it takes in no more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְזוּפָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from רב נחמן's to the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה through how casks work, without narrowing it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a pitch-coated cask could absorb nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any old cask that is already soaked absorbs no more.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even refined oil gets a sediment deduction
steps.stepSummary: The משנה quotes רבי יהודה: even when selling refined oil all year round, the buyer accepts a deduction of a לוג and a half of sediment per hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: even someone who sells refined oil to another all year round, the buyer accepts a deduction of a לוג and a half of sediment for every hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the משנה, which is רבי יהודה's view about refined oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the חכמים said that with refined oil there is no sediment deduction. רבי יהודה disagrees: even with clean, refined oil, the standard sediment deduction still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Refined, filtered oil with no sediment
Sediment, the dregs at the bottom of the barrel
A לוג and a half per hundred, the standard sediment measure

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even one who sells refined oil to his fellow
all the days of the year,
this buyer accepts upon himself
a log and a half of sediment for every hundred.
phrases.notes: He means a hundred לוג of oil. The seller may take off a לוג and a half of that amount for sediment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמּוֹכֵר שֶׁמֶן מְזוּקָּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the side discussion about casks absorbing oil, and quotes רבי יהודה's dissent from the ruling in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, even refined oil carries the standard sediment deduction of a לוג and a half per hundred.

steps.title: אביי: the dispute is about mixing sediment into oil
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that, when you look into it, רבי יהודה must hold that mixing sediment into oil is allowed, and the חכמים must hold that it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: when you look into it, you will find that according to רבי יהודה it is permitted to mix sediment into oil, and according to the חכמים it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the reason behind the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי ties the sediment deduction to a deeper question: may a seller mix the dregs back into the oil and sell it all as oil? If mixing is allowed, the seller has a strong claim to the deduction. If it is forbidden, he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: When you look into it, you will find it must be said

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When you look into it, you will find that you must say,

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מוּתָּר לְעָרֵב שְׁמָרִים,
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yehuda, it is permitted to mix sediment into the oil,
according to the Rabbis, it is forbidden to mix sediment into the oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the argument in the משנה really depends on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה permits mixing sediment into oil; the חכמים forbid it.

steps.title: Why the buyer must accept the deduction according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה allows mixing, the seller can tell the buyer: 'I could have mixed the sediment in, so accept the deduction now.'
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה it is permitted to mix sediment, and that is why the buyer accepts the deduction. The seller says to him: if I wanted to mix it in for you, couldn't I? So now too, accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats אביי's words about רבי יהודה and spells out how they explain the buyer's acceptance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller's claim is: 'I had the right to sell you sediment mixed in as oil. Instead I gave you clean oil, so accept the deduction I would have had anyway.' This explanation is what the next questions will attack.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מוּתָּר לְעָרֵב שְׁמָרִים,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda, it is permitted to mix sediment,
and that is the reason the buyer accepts the deduction,
because the seller says to him:
If I had wanted to mix it in for you,
couldn't I have mixed it in for you?
So now too, accept the deduction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands אביי's statement into the seller's actual argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the seller could have mixed the sediment in, so the buyer must accept the deduction even for refined oil.

steps.title: But mixed sediment could be resold, and plain sediment cannot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the buyer can answer that mixed-in sediment could have been resold, while sediment alone is useless to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the buyer say to him: if you had mixed it in, I could have sold it. Now what will I do with it? On its own, I can't sell it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the seller's argument from step 12 by giving the buyer a strong reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mixing and deducting are not equal. Sediment mixed into the oil passes on to the next customer, so the buyer loses nothing. Sediment counted separately is a real loss, because nobody buys plain dregs.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But let the buyer say to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי עָרֵבְתְּ לֵיהּ – הֲוָה מִזְדַּבַּן לִי,
phrases.english: If you had mixed it in, I could have sold it,
now what will I do with it?
On its own, I can't sell it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the seller's claim from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The seller's argument 'I could have mixed it in, so accept the deduction.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mixed sediment can be passed on to the buyer's own customers. Deducted sediment is a pure loss, so the two are not the same.

steps.title: The buyer is a homeowner who wants clear oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is a homeowner buying oil for his own use, who prefers clean oil anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are dealing with a homeowner, who prefers clear oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing down who the buyer is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A homeowner is not reselling the oil, so the 'I could have passed it on' argument does not apply to him. For him, clean oil is actually better, so he gains from the seller not mixing.

keyTerms.meaning: A homeowner, buying for his own use and not a merchant

phrases.english: We are dealing with a homeowner,
who prefers clear oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific type of buyer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyer is a merchant who could resell mixed sediment, so the deduction is a loss to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer is a homeowner who uses the oil himself and prefers it clear, so not mixing helps him.

steps.title: By not mixing, didn't the seller give it up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the buyer can say that by not mixing, the seller gave up his right to the sediment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the buyer say to him: since you did not mix it in for me, you clearly gave it up to me!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to the seller's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the seller had the right to mix, he chose not to. The buyer claims this choice shows the seller gave up (מחל) his right to charge for sediment.

keyTerms.meaning: You surely gave it up / forgave it
From the fact that you did not

phrases.english: But let the buyer say to him:
Since you did not mix it in for me,
you clearly gave it up to me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 settled the first challenge, a new challenge attacks the same seller argument from another side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The seller's claim to the deduction in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seller's choice not to mix should be read as giving up his right to the sediment.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does not assume a person gave something up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה follows his own view: we do not assume that someone gave something up unless he said so.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, since he does not hold of assumed forgiveness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge by pointing to רבי יהודה's general approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer's claim rests on guessing that the seller gave up his right. רבי יהודה does not accept such guesses, so the seller keeps his right to the deduction. The next step brings a source for this approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Follows his own reasoning, consistent with his other rulings

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
since he does not accept giving up a right.
phrases.notes: He means we can't just assume the seller gave something up. He would have had to say so.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מְחִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to the author's consistent general principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Not mixing shows the seller gave up his right to the sediment.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה does not assume מחילה, so the seller keeps his right to the deduction.

steps.title: Source: selling the yoke versus selling the cattle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: selling the yoke does not include the cattle, and selling the cattle does not include the yoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: if he sold him the yoke, he did not sell him the cattle. If he sold him the cattle, he did not sell him the yoke.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show where we see that רבי יהודה does not assume מחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sale includes only exactly what was named, and nothing extra is assumed to come along. In the same way, we do not assume the oil seller gave up anything he did not clearly give up.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The yoke that joins a pair of plowing animals

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, a buyer of refined oil still accepts the sediment deduction. The seller could have mixed the sediment in, the buyer is a homeowner who prefers clear oil, and רבי יהודה never assumes someone gave up a right.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If he sold him the yoke,
he did not sell him the cattle.
If he sold him the cattle,
he did not sell him the yoke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 16 that רבי יהודה does not assume מחילה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not assume someone gave up a right
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בבא בתרא: selling the yoke does not include the cattle, and selling the cattle does not include the yoke.

steps.title: The price tells us what was sold
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the משנה: רבי יהודה says the price shows what was meant. The חכמים say the price is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the price tells us what was sold. How so? If someone says, 'Sell me your צמד for two hundred זוז,' everyone knows a yoke is not worth two hundred זוז, so he must mean the cattle. The חכמים say: the price is no proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it began in the last step. This is the proof that רבי יהודה does not assume someone gave up money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the deal by the price. If the price is too high for a yoke, the buyer must have meant the cattle, because we do not assume he overpaid on purpose. The חכמים say the price proves nothing, since one side may have given up the difference. So רבי יהודה does not assume people give things up, while the חכמים do.

keyTerms.meaning: The price tells us (what the sale included)
A yoke, or a pair of yoked cattle

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole argument that follows. רבי יהודה does not assume a person gave something up, but the חכמים are willing to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the price tells us.
How so?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מְכוֹר לִי צִמְדְּךָ בְּמָאתַיִם זוּז –
phrases.english: If he said to him: Sell me your tzemed for two hundred zuz,
phrases.notes: The word צמד can mean the yoke or the pair of cattle. That is why it is unclear what was sold.

phrases.aramaic: הַדָּבָר יָדוּעַ שֶׁאֵין הַצֶּמֶד בְּמָאתַיִים זוּז.
phrases.english: it is well known that a yoke does not cost two hundred zuz.
And the Rabbis say: the price is not proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quoted in step 17, which supports step 16's claim about רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה does not assume a person gave up money unless he said so.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on selling a צמד: רבי יהודה goes by the price, while the חכמים say the price is no proof.

steps.title: אביי's reading of the חכמים' view
steps.stepSummary: According to the חכמים, mixing sediment is forbidden. So the buyer refuses a sediment deduction: since you could not have mixed it in, I don't accept it now either.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the חכמים, it is forbidden to mix sediment into oil. That is why the buyer refuses the deduction. He tells the seller: if you had wanted to mix it in, would you have been allowed? So now too, I don't accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to finish אביי's explanation, now giving the חכמים' side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the seller was never allowed to sell sediment as oil. So he cannot make the buyer pay for it through a deduction either. The buyer gets clean oil and no sediment is counted against him.

keyTerms.meaning: To mix sediment into the oil

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, it is forbidden to mix in sediment,
and this is the reason that he does not accept,
phrases.notes: He means the buyer does not accept having the sediment taken off what he receives.

phrases.english: because he says to him: if you had wanted to mix it in,
would you have been allowed?
Now too, I don't accept it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof about רבי יהודה, returns to complete אביי's statement with the חכמים' side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, mixing is forbidden, so the buyer does not have to accept a sediment deduction.

steps.title: רב פפא flips the חכמים' view
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the opposite makes more sense. The חכמים permit mixing, and the buyer refuses because by not mixing, the seller gave up his right to the sediment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: On the contrary, the opposite makes sense! According to the חכמים, mixing sediment is allowed. The buyer refuses the deduction because he says: since you didn't mix it in for me, you gave it up to me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges אביי by reversing which side permits mixing. Here he starts with the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים are the ones who say people do give things up, as the צמד משנה showed. So רב פפא says their reason fits 'you gave it up,' not 'it's forbidden.' This means the חכמים can permit mixing and still free the buyer from the deduction.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
On the contrary, the opposite makes sense!
According to the Rabbis, it is permitted to mix in sediment,
and this is the reason he does not accept,
because he says to him: since you didn't mix it in for me,
you must have given it up to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: אַדְּרַבָּה, אִיפְּכָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against אביי's reading in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's assignment of views: that רבי יהודה permits mixing sediment and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים hold that people give things up (step 18). So their reason for freeing the buyer should be that the seller gave up the sediment, which only works if mixing is permitted.

steps.title: רב פפא: for רבי יהודה the buyer must accept
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids mixing. So the buyer must accept the deduction, because otherwise the seller makes no profit, and a merchant has to earn something.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה, mixing sediment is forbidden. That is why the buyer must accept the deduction. The seller tells him: I am not allowed to mix it in for you. If you won't accept the deduction either, I gain nothing. Is someone who buys and sells at the same price called a merchant?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his reversed reading by explaining רבי יהודה's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה forbids mixing, the seller has only one way to earn something: the sediment deduction. Without it, he would sell at cost. A merchant who sells at the price he paid isn't really doing business, so the buyer has to accept the deduction.

keyTerms.meaning: Buy and sell (at the same price)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: חכמים forbid mixing (so no deduction), and רבי יהודה permits it. רב פפא: חכמים permit mixing (no deduction, because of מחילה), and רבי יהודה forbids it (so there is a deduction, so the merchant can profit).

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָסוּר לְעָרֵב שְׁמָרִים,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda, it is forbidden to mix in sediment,
and this is the reason that he accepts,
because he says to him: if I wanted to mix it in,
I am not allowed to mix it in for you,
and you won't accept the deduction either?
Is one who buys and sells at the same price called a merchant?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָסוּר לְעָרֵב שְׁמָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's reversed reading, now for רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה (as רב פפא reads him), mixing is forbidden and the buyer must accept the sediment deduction so the seller can profit.

steps.title: A buyer and a depositor are the same regarding residue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a buyer and a person who deposits oil are treated alike regarding פקטים (residue in the oil).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a buyer and one who deposits oil are the same regarding residue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It is short and unclear, which sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares two cases: someone buying oil, and someone leaving oil with a שומר. It says they are the same 'regarding residue' but does not say how. The גמרא will now try to figure that out.

keyTerms.meaning: One who deposits an item with someone to guard
Residue in oil, such as floating bits of olive

phrases.english: It was taught: both the buyer
and the one who deposits are the same regarding residue.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא: אֶחָד הַלּוֹקֵחַ וְאֶחָד הַמַּפְקִיד לִפְקָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source related to deductions from oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer and a depositor of oil are treated alike regarding residue.

steps.title: What does 'regarding residue' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means. Its first guess: just as a buyer doesn't accept a residue deduction, the depositor doesn't either.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'regarding residue' mean? If you say it means that just as the buyer doesn't accept a deduction for residue, the depositor also doesn't accept a deduction for residue...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the ברייתא and offers a first suggestion. The challenge to that suggestion comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first guess is that the depositor is like the buyer. Neither has residue taken off the amount they get back. So the שומר would have to return the full amount of oil.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a suggestion that will be challenged)

phrases.english: What does 'regarding residue' mean?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵימָא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלוֹקֵחַ לָא מְקַבֵּל פְּקָטִים,
phrases.english: If you say: just as the buyer does not accept residue,
so too the depositor does not accept residue,
phrases.notes: He means the owner does not accept getting back less oil because of the residue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא in step 22 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the same for the buyer and the depositor regarding residue?

steps.title: Challenge: what would the guard do with the residue?
steps.stepSummary: The guard can say: what am I supposed to do with your residue? It came from your own oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the guard say to him: your residue, what should I do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first suggestion. The שומר should not have to replace oil lost as residue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer can refuse residue because he paid for clean oil. A שומר, though, just guarded the owner's oil. The residue was part of that same oil, so the שומר did nothing wrong. This makes it hard to say the depositor is like the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him (introduces a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: פְּקָטָךְ מַאי אֶיעְבֵּיד לְהוּ?
phrases.english: But let him say to him: your residue, what should I do with it?
phrases.notes: The one speaking is the guard who held the oil, talking to the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: פְּקָטָךְ מַאי אֶיעְבֵּיד לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested meaning in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the depositor, like the buyer, gets no residue deduction.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The residue came from the owner's own oil. The guard did not cause it, so he should not have to make it up.

steps.title: New reading: the buyer accepts residue just like the depositor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is read the other way around. Just as a depositor accepts a deduction for residue, a buyer does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא means: just as the depositor accepts residue, the buyer also accepts residue.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first reading of the ברייתא was rejected, the גמרא gives a new reading of what 'buyer and depositor are alike' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guard was right that he can't be blamed for residue that came from the owner's own oil. So the depositor does accept the loss. The ברייתא's comparison must therefore mean the buyer also accepts a residue deduction.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who deposits an item with a guard
Residue or dregs mixed into the oil

phrases.english: Rather, just as the depositor
accepts residue,
the buyer also accepts residue.
phrases.notes: 'Accepts' means he takes back less oil, because the residue is deducted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּמַפְקִיד מְקַבֵּל פְּקָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first reading, which step 24 rejected
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the ברייתא's comparison of buyer and depositor means
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both of them accept a deduction for residue

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יהודה: the buyer does not accept residue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying that the buyer takes a deduction only for sediment, without residue. This contradicts the new reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a buyer really accept residue? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: the rule about murky oil was said only for the seller, because the buyer accepts a deduction of a לוג and a half of sediment but not residue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading with a ברייתא that says the buyer does not have to accept a residue deduction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the loss from murky oil falls on the seller. The buyer only absorbs the fixed deduction for sediment. That seems to directly contradict the claim that 'the buyer accepts residue.'

keyTerms.meaning: Sediment at the bottom of the barrel
A לוג and a half, the fixed sediment deduction
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But does a buyer accept residue?
But isn't it taught: רבי יהודה says:
They did not speak of murky oil
except for the seller alone,
phrases.notes: He means the loss from murky oil falls only on the seller.

phrases.english: for the buyer accepts upon himself
a לוג and a half of sediment, without residue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new reading from step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a buyer accepts a residue deduction
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's ברייתא says the buyer takes only the sediment deduction, not residue

steps.title: Paying in תשרי versus paying in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: Two different cases. If the buyer paid in תשרי at the תשרי price, he accepts residue. If he paid in ניסן at the ניסן price, he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No difficulty. One ברייתא is about a buyer who paid in תשרי and collects in ניסן according to the תשרי measure. The other is about a buyer who paid in ניסן and collects in ניסן according to the ניסן measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות describe different deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תשרי, right after the harvest, oil is cheap and murky. A buyer who locked in the תשרי price agreed to oil as it is then, residue and all. A buyer who paid in ניסן expects clear oil, so the residue loss stays with the seller.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of the olive harvest, when oil is murky and cheap
A spring month, when the oil has settled and become clear

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a buyer takes the residue loss depends on the deal. Buying at the cheap תשרי price means accepting murky oil. Buying at the ניסן price means expecting clear oil.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he gave him money in תשרי
and takes from him in ניסן
according to the measure of תשרי.
phrases.notes: He gets oil counted the way it was in תשרי, when it was still murky.

phrases.english: That is where he gave him money in ניסן
and takes from him in ניסן
according to the measure of ניסן.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ זוּזֵי בְּתִשְׁרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seem to disagree about whether a buyer accepts residue
steps.terutzMaskana: A buyer at the תשרי price accepts residue. A buyer at the ניסן price does not.

steps.title: משנה: a moved barrel breaks when the owner chose no spot
steps.stepSummary: A guard moves a deposited barrel that had no assigned spot. If it breaks in his hand, he pays only if he moved it for his own use. If it breaks after he put it down, he is exempt either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone deposits a barrel with a friend and the owner did not choose a spot for it, and the guard moved it and it broke: if it broke in his hand, he is liable if he moved it for his own need and exempt if he moved it for the barrel's need. If it broke after he put it down, he is exempt either way.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses a guard who moves a barrel he is watching. This step covers the case where the owner did not assign it a spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving it for his own use is like taking it for himself, so he is responsible while holding it. Once he puts it back down, he is no longer responsible, even if he first moved it for his own use. Moving it to protect the barrel never makes him liable.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the endings: לְצוֹרְכּוֹ (his need, the guard) versus לְצוֹרְכָּהּ (her need, the barrel). One letter changes the whole ruling.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who deposits a barrel with his fellow
and the owners did not designate a place for it,
and he moved it and it broke:
if it broke while in his hand,
for his own need, he is liable;
for its need, he is exempt.
If it broke after he put it down,
whether for his need or for its need, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With no assigned spot, he is liable only if it breaks in his hand after he moved it for his own need. Once he puts it down, he is exempt.

steps.title: משנה: a moved barrel breaks when the owner chose a spot
steps.stepSummary: If the owner assigned a spot and the guard moved the barrel, he is liable even after he puts it down, but only if he moved it for his own need.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner chose a spot for it, and the guard moved it and it broke, whether in his hand or after he put it down: if for his own need, he is liable; if for its need, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the second case, where the owner did choose a spot for the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference from step 28 is the case where it breaks after he put it down. Here putting it down does not free him, because he did not return it to the spot the owner chose. Moving it for the barrel's own good still exempts him.
steps.whatToRemember: With no assigned spot, putting the barrel down ends the guard's liability. With an assigned spot, it does not. In every case, moving it for the barrel's sake means he is exempt.

phrases.english: If the owners designated a place for it,
and he moved it and it broke,
whether while in his hand or after he put it down:
for his own need, he is liable;
for its need, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the משנה, contrasting with step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With an assigned spot, moving it for his own need makes him liable whether it breaks in his hand or after he puts it down.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking whose view it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The focus is the ruling in step 28. The guard moved the barrel for himself, which is like taking it, then put it down without telling the owner, and he is still exempt. Not everyone agrees that putting something back without the owner knowing counts, so the גמרא wants to know who holds this.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Whose is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the משנה's ruling follows

steps.title: It follows רבי ישמעאל: the owner does not need to know
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, who holds that returning an item does not require the owner's knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי ישמעאל, who says we do not need the owner's knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that putting a taken item back counts as returning it even if the owner never finds out. That explains why the guard in step 28 is exempt once he puts the barrel down.

phrases.english: It is רבי ישמעאל,
who says: we do not require the owner's knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא, דְּאָמַר: לָא בָּעִינַן דַּעַת בְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, who does not require the owner's knowledge for a return

steps.title: The ברייתא about returning a stolen lamb or coin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי ישמעאל's view: a thief returns a stolen lamb or coin to the place he took it from. The גמרא then begins quoting רבי עקיבא, who disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: one who steals a lamb from the flock or a סלע from the purse should return it to the place he stole it from. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי ישמעאל's opinion. It starts introducing רבי עקיבא's opposing view, which continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל lets the thief simply put the item back where it was, without informing the owner. This is the same idea that exempts the guard once he puts the barrel down. רבי עקיבא's disagreement is only introduced here.

phrases.english: As it is taught: one who steals a lamb from the flock
or a סלע from the purse,
should return it to the place he stole it from,
these are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
רבי עקיבא says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the opinion named in step 31
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל does not require the owner's knowledge for a return
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a thief returning a stolen lamb or coin to its place
